appraisal_events.evidence: M. de Stermaria n'était pas ce jour-là à Balbec, au grand regret du bâtonnier. Mais insidieusement il dit au maître d'hôtel : « Aimé, vous pourrez dire à M. de Stermaria qu'il n'est pas le seul noble qu'il y ait dans cette salle à manger... c'est le marquis de Cambremer. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The bâtonnier's vanity escalates from performing modesty for his card-playing friends to orchestrating, through the head waiter, that word of his aristocratic lunch reach M. de Stermaria, whom he regrets not being present to impress directly; the narrator's 'insidieusement' marks this as calculated status-seeking.

status_effects.explanation: He is exposed as an eager status-seeker, scheming to have his brush with nobility relayed to another nobleman he was not even present to impress in person.
